Tom's Hardware found the RTX 5090 FE the fastest GPU they've tested "most of the time," with 32GB GDDR7 on a 512-bit bus and potent AI performance. Downsides listed: driver issues in some games and apps, extreme price and power, availability concerns. They later docked half a star specifically because the Founders Edition runs hot.

Reviewer caution on Multi Frame Generation: it adds latency, and MFG showing 240 FPS means user input is only sampled at 60 FPS. That is not the same as a game like Counter-Strike 2 running at 240 FPS natively.

TechPowerUp notes the Founders Edition is as long and tall as the 4090 FE but only 2 slots thick versus 3. Power hits 575 W, near the limit of the 600 W 12V-2x6 connector. The $1,999 price is a steep increase over the 4090's $1,599.

Commenter criticizes the 12VHPWR setup on 5090 FE cards. Pins feed a bus bar on a single 12V plane, so current balance relies entirely on contact resistance, with no per-pin shunts or active balancing. By contrast, older 8-pin designs metered and balanced current across connectors.

Referencing a Reddit thread about an RTX 5090 FE with a molten 12VHPWR connector, a user notes that people there blamed the owner for using a "third party" connector. Another says Nvidia doubled down on a flawed design, and the short adapter still leaves a mess of cables in the case.

User points out that Nvidia made an amazingly small 5090 FE, but none of the board partners followed suit. So most customers see no benefit from the small connector, since 600W cards need huge coolers anyway.
Summary from a commenter on Llama.cpp benchmarks: performance isn't bad, but perf per watt isn't better than the 4080 or 4090. In certain contexts it can be significantly lower than the 4090.

Local-LLM hobbyist says that if RTX 5090 prices stay around 3500€, the card will remain insignificant for the DIY crowd, who favor used 3090s for VRAM per dollar. They acknowledge FP4 support and speed matter more for long reasoning-model outputs.
From Phoronix Linux compute tests, as discussed: across 60+ CUDA/OptiX/OpenCL/Vulkan benchmarks the 5090 delivered 1.42x the RTX 4090's performance. Power efficiency was similar to the 4080/4090.

Commenter reasons the 5090 is worth about 1.33x a 4090: ~1.4x performance and 1.33x VRAM, but ~1.4x power, so the 4090 remains a reasonable option. They worry that running the die at 500W+ concentrates a lot of heat and may shorten its lifetime.

User says the 5090 is unobtainium, available only from absurdly priced eBay scalpers. They switched to combining multiple lesser cards and got a mix of Intel and Nvidia cards working on one inference job after two days of fiddling.
At $2,000 base and $5-7k scalper prices, one commenter says the 5090 is out of reach for most people and plans to keep using their 3000-series card until it dies.
Commenter defends GPU pricing using the benchmarks: compared to the GTX 980 (inflation-adjusted), the 5090 costs about 2.7x as much but delivers about 14.3x the performance.
Reader notes the 4080 Super trails the 5080 and 5090 in many tests but appears to have a better performance-per-watt ratio than both, while also running at some of the lowest temps.
